plants.name: Crocus sativus
plants.description: Delicate lilac goblets streaked with violet veins open at dawn. Each one holds three crimson threads, the stigmas that become saffron, the world's most prized spice. Whole fields turn a soft purple for a few short weeks.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-October to November in most regions, with early flowers appearing in late September in cooler or higher-elevation areas
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe and Southwest Asia, including Spain's La Mancha and Iran's Khorasan region
plants.funFact: It takes roughly 150 flowers to yield just one gram of dried saffron, and every stigma is picked by hand.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale pink-lilac, chalice-shaped blooms push straight out of bare ground in damp meadows and woodland edges. They appear with no leaves, which gives them the nickname 'naked ladies'. The leaves come up the following spring.
plants.location: Meadows and open woodlands across Central and Western Europe, including the UK, Germany and Switzerland
plants.funFact: Despite the name, it is not a true crocus. It is highly toxic, but its compound colchicine is also used in medicine and in plant breeding.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: Tall plumes of tiny golden flowers arch above roadsides, prairies and field edges, and bees and butterflies crowd them in the last warm days of the season. Whole hillsides look as if they have been dusted with sunlight.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late July to October, peaking in September
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from the Great Lakes to the Northeast United States and southern Canada
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but its pollen is heavy and sticky and is carried by insects. The usual culprit is ragweed, which blooms at the same time.
